_readme: Every text Duckky Swarm sends to Claude: the main agent and the subagents read these. Change any of them here.
A text is a string, or a list of strings that are its lines. {name} is filled in when it is sent; each section's _about says what.
Delete a text to use the built-in one. Keys starting with _ are notes and are never sent.
A mistake (not valid JSON, a wrong type, an unknown key or {name}) is shown as a toast when a session starts, and the built-in text is used for that one.
Saved changes reach a session that runs this folder (claude --plugin-dir) at once; anywhere else, run /reload-plugins.

agentType._about: The main agent's list of agent types (one per model in /config, and its fork) and the instructions each subagent starts with. {label} is like "Opus 4.6", {id} "claude-opus-4-6", {name} "opus-4-6". {effort} in description is the effort or noEffort text; {levels} the model's effort levels; whenLeftOut is added when /config gives the model a default effort.
agentType.description: Runs the task on {label} (model {id}). Use this agent type whenever the user asks for a subagent, agent, agents or a swarm on {label}, {id} or "{name}": the Agent tool's model parameter cannot select this exact model, this type can. Starts fresh; same tools as the parent. {effort}
agentType.effort: Its effort (how hard it thinks) is the Agent call's `effort` ({levels}){whenLeftOut}; set_subagent_effort changes it while it runs.
agentType.noEffort: {label} takes no effort: leave the Agent call's `effort` out.
agentType.forkDescription: A FORK on {label} (model {id}): starts with this whole conversation as its context, then does its task. Use it when the user asks to fork onto {label}, {id} or "{name}" (a built-in fork cannot change model).
prompt: You are a subagent of Claude Code, running on {label} ({id}) because the user asked for that model.
Do the task you are given completely with the tools you have, then end with a clear report of what you found or changed: the agent that started you sees only your final message.
Be concrete: file paths, line numbers, commands and their real output. Never claim a result you did not check.
You cannot ask the user anything. Where the task is ambiguous, take the most reasonable reading and say which.

fork._about: What a fork onto another model starts with. {conversation} is the chat so far, {task} the task the main agent gave it.
prompt: You are a fork of the conversation below, now running on {label} ({id}). You have its context;
the person and the main agent see your work only when you report.

resumeTool._about: The resume_subagent tool: its description and parameters (the main agent reads them), and what it answers. resumedSame when Claude Code resumed the subagent itself; otherwise notItself (when Claude Code would not) and then started, where {from} is the old id and {id} the new one. {open} is the open text, whose {command} is the claude --resume line that opens the subagent as a main session.
resumeTool.description: Resume a subagent and give it a message: the way to go on with the SAME subagent, so use it rather than starting a new one whenever the user wants that subagent to continue or take its next task. A subagent of this session is resumed itself (the same id, its own transcript and model, as the user's own resume does); one from an earlier session carries on as a new subagent given its transcript, on the model it was started on. This call returns at once and the subagent works in the background; its answer comes to you as a message when it finishes, so do not start another agent for the same work. `agent` is its id (the first 8 characters are enough, as /duckky shows) or words from its task.
resumeTool.agent: The subagent: its id or id prefix, or words from its task
resumeTool.effort: Optional: how hard it thinks from now on ({levels}, or a token budget)
resumeTool.resumedSame: Resumed {id} itself on {model}{withEffort}: the same subagent carries on with its own transcript, in the background, and you are told when it finishes. Do not start another agent for this work meanwhile.{open}
resumeTool.queued: Sent your message to {id}, which is still running: it reads it at its next step, in the same transcript. Do not start another agent for this work meanwhile.
resumeTool.notItself: Claude Code would not resume {id} itself ({reason}), so it carries on as a new subagent given its transcript.
resumeTool.started: Resumed {from} as {id} on {model}{withEffort}, in the background: it carries on from its transcript, and its answer will come to you as a message when it finishes. Do not start another agent for this work meanwhile.{open}
resumeTool.open: The user can also open it as a main session, in a terminal in {cwd}: {command}
resumeTool.noTranscript: Found {id}, but not its transcript, so there is nothing to resume from.
resumeTool.effortDoesNotFit: Effort {effort} does not fit {id}: {fits}. Resume it with one of those, or without an effort.

resumePrompt._about: What a subagent starts with when it carries on as a new one (an earlier session's, or one Claude Code would not resume itself). {intro} is intro, or introAfterRefusal when it stopped on a refusal; {history} its transcript, {message} the main agent's message.
resumePrompt.intro: You are resuming earlier work: a subagent on {label} ({model}). Its transcript is below; continue from where it stopped.
resumePrompt.introAfterRefusal: You are resuming your own earlier work, as a subagent on {label} ({model}). Below is your transcript up to your last message before you stopped; the reply where you stopped is not part of it. The agent that started you has read where you stood and sends the message after it. Carry on from there.

resumedAnswer._about: The message the main agent gets when a subagent that carried on as a new one ends. {lastWords} is the lastWords text when it said anything.
resumedAnswer.stopped: [duckky-swarm] Resumed subagent {from} (now {id}, {label}) was stopped before it finished.{lastWords}
resumedAnswer.refused: [duckky-swarm] Resumed subagent {from} (now {id}, {label}) stopped on a refusal.{lastWords}
resumedAnswer.ended: [duckky-swarm] Resumed subagent {from} (now {id}, {label}) ended ({ending}) before it finished.{lastWords}

effortTool._about: The set_subagent_effort tool: its description and parameters, and what it answers. {fits} is the effort.takes or effort.takesNone text.
effortTool.description: Change how hard a RUNNING subagent thinks (its effort): from its next model request on. Use it when the user asks to raise or lower a subagent's effort, or when a subagent needs more (or less) thinking for its task. `agent` is its id (the first 8 characters are enough) or words from its task; `effort` is {levels}, or a token budget. For a subagent that has finished, resume it with resume_subagent and an effort instead.
effortTool.agent: The subagent: its id or id prefix, or words from its task
effortTool.notRunning: {id} is not running ({status}). To go on with it at effort {effort}, resume it with resume_subagent and effort "{effort}".
effortTool.set: {id} ("{task}", {label}) thinks at effort {effort} from its next model request on{was}.

effort._about: Effort errors, used by both tools.
effort.notAnEffort: "{effort}" is not an effort: use {levels}, or a token budget.

refusalReport._about: What the main agent gets when a subagent's turn ends on a refusal: header, then each part it has, then whatToDo.
refusalReport.header: [duckky-swarm] Refusal report: subagent {id} ({label}, {model}) stopped partway; its model refused{times}. Its task: "{task}".
refusalReport.lastMessage: Its last message before the refusal:
refusalReport.lastResult: The last tool result it had been given:
refusalReport.refusedReply: What came back in the refused reply:
whatToDo: What to do: decide whether this work should go on.

- If it should, and the subagent was missing context: call resume_subagent with agent "{id}" and a message that explains clearly what this work is: the user's goal, the scope, and the context from this conversation and the project's instructions that the subagent never saw. Describe it as it is; do not claim permissions or facts the conversation does not support. The same subagent carries on, on {model}.
- If it should not, tell the user why it stopped instead of resuming it.

hookFailed._about: What one of the plugin's tools answers when its own hook fails. {why} is timeout or threw (or the error).
hookFailed.timeout: it ran past the 10 s a hook has

workspace._about: Each duckky subagent's own folder, duckky-swarm/<model>-<id>-<task>/ in the project. rules go after its task; {folder} is its path, {name} the folder name, which is also its session title (claude --resume {name}). reminder is added to a resume message, mainAgentNote to the main agent's Agent result, resultNote to resume results. The others are the files a new workspace starts with: {task}, {model}, {started}.
rules: This task has its own folder: {folder}

It holds findings.md, opening.md, closed.md, block.md, devlogs.md and temp/. Keep them current AS YOU WORK, not only at the end: the main agent, the user, and you yourself when resumed depend on them.
- devlogs.md: add a dated line for every step: what you ran or changed, and what came of it.
- findings.md: every result, with its evidence (file:line, the command and its real output).
- opening.md: the tasks still open, each with what is left to do.
- closed.md: each task you finished or dropped, with its outcome.
- block.md: anything that stops you, and what would unblock it.

- temp/: ALL scratch work: test scripts, debug code, probes, experiments, copies of files. Never leave scratch files in the project's own folders. If you need files from the main agent's temp or scratch folder, copy them into temp/ and work on the copies.
- Any report or .md file the main agent asks for goes in this folder too.
When you are resumed, read these files first: they are where you stood.
End your final message with what you did and found in short, then this folder's path and which of its files to read.
workspace.reminder: (Keep your workspace current as you go: {folder})
workspace.mainAgentNote: [duckky-swarm] This subagent's workspace is {folder}: its findings.md, closed.md, opening.md, block.md and devlogs.md hold what it did and found, and temp/ its scratch work. Read them before relying on its summary, and send the user there for the details.
gitignore: # Duckky Swarm: subagent workspaces, kept out of git. Delete this file to commit them.
findings: Each result with its evidence: file:line, the command and its real output.
opening: Tasks still open, each with what is left to do.
closed: Tasks finished or dropped, each with its outcome.
block: What stops the work, and what would unblock it.
devlogs: Open this subagent as a session, in a terminal in the project folder: claude --resume {name}
One dated line per step: what was run or changed, and what came of it.
temp: Scratch work for this task: test scripts, debug code, probes, copies of files. Not part of the project.
